title: Rapid poverty reduction can coexist with informal job creation, spatial concentration, gendered care exclusion, and a thinner safety net
source_unit: World Bank Uzbekistan Poverty and Equity Assessment, Rising to Prosperity: Broadening Opportunities for All, disclosed September 18, 2026
geography: Uzbekistan, 2021-2025 poverty, labor-market, spatial, gender, human-capital, and social-protection analysis

poverty_decline.value: National poverty fell from 17.0% to 5.8%, lifting approximately 3.7 million people out of poverty

middle_class.value: The middle-class share more than doubled to over 72% of the population, while one in five people remains vulnerable to falling back into poverty

drivers.value: Rising wage employment and higher wage earnings drove most of the reported poverty reduction

observations.method: World Bank Poverty and Equity Assessment using household welfare, labor-market, and distributional analysis; the reported poverty and middle-class changes are not a randomized intervention estimate.
observations.uncertainty: Poverty-line choice, survey comparability, consumption and income measurement, price adjustment, vulnerability thresholds, and attribution among wage, employment, remittance, and policy changes shape the estimates.
observations.subgroup: Poor, vulnerable, middle-class, urban, rural, regional, gender, and labor-market groups within Uzbekistan.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large poverty decline can represent genuine welfare improvement even if vulnerability remains; middle-class classification does not guarantee secure assets, quality work, or political voice.

observations.period: 2021-2025; job quantity, quality, and spatial concentration

new_job_composition.value: About two-thirds of new jobs are in construction and trade and about 85% are informal

productivity.value: Real labor productivity turned negative despite robust job creation

spatial_concentration.value: Half of high-skilled jobs are located in Tashkent city and region, and the capital's upper-middle-class population grew more than fourfold since 2021

observations.method: World Bank labor-market, spatial, and welfare analysis connecting employment growth to formality, productivity, skills, and location.
observations.uncertainty: The report's measures do not alone establish job duration, earnings distribution, working conditions, commuting, migration decisions, or causal effects of regional policy.
observations.subgroup: Construction and trade workers, informal workers, high-skilled workers, Tashkent and non-Tashkent regions, young people, and households deciding whether to migrate for opportunity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Informal jobs can provide vital entry and income when formal opportunities are scarce; negative productivity growth may reflect measurement, sector composition, or a temporary transition rather than permanent job deterioration.

observations.period: 2021-2025; gendered care, education, and social-protection gaps

care_exclusion.value: Among inactive adults in poor and vulnerable households, 92% are women, most citing care responsibilities; mothers of children under two are 36% less likely to work

gender_pay_gap.value: Women face a persistent reported gender wage gap of 35-40%

learning_and_safety_net.value: About 80% of 15-year-olds do not reach minimum proficiency in core subjects, while flagship cash-transfer coverage fell from 26% to 8% of households between 2022 and 2025

observations.method: World Bank gender, human-capital, and social-protection analysis within the Poverty and Equity Assessment; the report does not provide a causal estimate of care, education, or transfer-coverage effects.
observations.uncertainty: Care responsibilities, wage gaps, learning proficiency, and transfer coverage may reflect selection, measurement, household composition, policy eligibility, and labor-market structure; the source does not establish why coverage declined or the welfare effect for each household.
observations.subgroup: Women in poor and vulnerable households, mothers of young children, adolescents, low-income families, regions with lower tertiary access, and households eligible for the Low Income Family Allowance.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower transfer coverage can reflect successful income growth or redesigned targeting for some households, while care exclusion and wage gaps may change as services and job structures evolve; headline national progress does not settle these subgroup paths.

related_sources.claim: Official World Bank document record for the assessment, report number 214948, disclosure date, and downloadable report.

boundary: This record captures a country-level distributional pattern in Uzbekistan: strong poverty and middle-class improvement alongside job-quality, spatial, gender, human-capital, and safety-net constraints. It does not establish causal effects, durable mobility, household-level trajectories, or a universal model of poverty reduction.
